soundness_flags.label: thm:tie-uniform-lan-transfer
soundness_flags.one_line: The feasible selector is run on \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), but the theorem only gives primitive numerical bounds and never assumes it is a legal member of \(\mathcal G_p\) almost surely; without nonempty endpoints and the required game-class conditions, the cited saddle/certificate construction is not defined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:tie-uniform-lan-transfer
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Two-sided Le Cam approximation, joint total-variation approximation of the statistic and estimated game, and expected primitive-game error are assumed rather than derived.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The feasible regret guarantee is conditional on \(\lambda_n\to0\), \(\gamma_n\to0\), the stated primitive-game control, and a legal estimated-game construction.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 4.2, Assumption 5 and Theorems 4–5; Conclusion, first extension paragraph
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper solves directionally differentiable bounds under convexity and centrosymmetry, gives a feasible plug-in result, and explicitly leaves directional differentiability with centrosymmetry dropped for future research.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Assumption 1; Section 3 minimax construction and Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats a convex centrosymmetric parameter space and derives an exact minimax-regret rule among all decision rules through a hardest one-dimensional subfamily/modulus construction.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Definition of nontrivial partial identification; main minimax-regret theorem and Appendix proof Steps 1–5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses open-set sign ambiguity, proves multiplicity in its stated regime, studies threshold-rule failure under conditions, and does not give a full unrestricted-correspondence classification.

The paper develops large-sample treatment-rule optimality using limits of experiments and minimax criteria; it is a baseline framework rather than a result on joint approximation with a data-dependent estimated game.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Require \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\in\mathcal G_p\) almost surely, or define an explicit measurable repair/projection into a bounded legal game class and add its error to \(\alpha_n\).

Turn the transfer result into an implementable first-rate result by deriving \(\gamma_n\), \(\alpha_n\), and the certificate tolerance for one named endpoint-estimation model, rather than leaving all three as abstract vanishing errors.

Add a finite-dimensional complexity or certified termination bound for the exchange procedure on a stated rational/polyhedral subclass, distinguishing the computational contribution from generic exchange convergence.

recommended_next_step: Revise the feasible-transfer theorem to make the estimated game legally constructible on every sample, then advance the repaired field-tier kernel to Stage 0.
